THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for disposal.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 28.02.2015 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VII at Bijapur, (for short 'tribunal') in MVC.no.193/2013, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VII at Bijapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Shivashankar H Manur, learned counsel for claimant - appellant submitted that this appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation and also for fastening liability upon insurer.

It was submitted that in an accident that occurred on 04.03.2012, claimant traveling on his motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-28/L-1853 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 from Malaghan to Kolhar sustained grievous injuries when driver of passenger Autorickshaw bearing registration no.KA-28/A-3329 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle.
Despite taking prolonged treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of Autorickshaw.

4. On contest, wherein only respondent no.2 - insurer filed objections denying claim petition averments and alleging violation of terms and conditions of policy, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW-1 and Dr.Sadashivappa S. Bedar as PW-2.
Exhibits P1 to P18 were marked.
On behalf of respondents, three witnesses were examined as RW-1 to RW-3 and Exhibits R1 to R7 were marked.

5. On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle by its driver and that claimant sustained injuries in NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 said accident and was entitled for compensation.

However, on finding that there was violation of policy condition as Autorickshaw was plying beyond geographical area limit of its permit, it absolved liability of insurer and passed award against owner.

2 6.

It was further submitted that though claimant was 18 years of age and earning Rs.8,000/- per month from business, tribunal considered monthly income as Rs.5,000/- and awarded inadequate compensation towards pain and suffering, loss of income during laid-up period, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses.
It was submitted that though as per deposition of PW-2, claimant had sustained permanent disability to extent of 20%, tribunal did not award any compensation towards future loss of income.
On said ground sought for modifying award.
7. On other hand, Shri Manvendra Reddy, learned counsel for respondent no.2 - insurer sought support award.

It was submitted that when claimant was alleging NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 loss of memory etc. due to head injury, it was incumbent upon him to have examined a Neurologist to establish loss of earning capacity.
However PW-2 - General Surgeon was examined to substantiate loss of earning capacity.
On noticing same, tribunal discarded evidence insofar as permanent disability and rightly refused to grant compensation towards future loss of income.
It was submitted that based on material on record, tribunal has passed appropriate award and same did not call for interference.

8. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
9.

From above submission, since claimant is challenging finding of tribunal regarding liability and is also seeking for enhancement of compensation, points that arise for consideration are:
i. Whether tribunal was justified in holding violation of terms and conditions of policy and consequently NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 holding only owner is liable to pay compensation?
 ii.
Whether claimant is entitled for  enhancement of compensation as  sought for?

Point no.1:
10.
In order to substantiate contentions regarding liability, it was submitted that Ex.P18 - Copy of permit did not contain any stipulation regarding geographical area.
However, endorsement at Ex.R2 relied upon by tribunal contained a condition regarding geographical limit i.e. 16 kms. from Vijayapura City Limits.
Tribunal referred to deposition of RW-2 - Assistant Executive Engineer of National Highway to conclude that accident spot was at distance of 27 kms. from limits of Vijayapura City.
Based on same, it concluded that there was violation of permit condition.

However, Division Bench of this Court in MFA.no.201648/2015 and connected matters disposed of on 26.11.2020, has held that even in case of violation of permit condition,
insurer would be squarely liable.
Ratio of NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 said decision would cover point no.(i).
Therefore, point no.(i) is held that finding of tribunal regarding liability would be contrary to law, same is modified by holding insurer liable to pay compensation.

3 Point no.(ii):
11.
Insofar as claim for enhancement, though claimant aged 19 years and stated to be earning Rs.8,000/- per month from business same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2012 is Rs.6,500/-, same has to be considered.
Insofar as disability, PW-2 assessed physical disability to extent of 20%.
However, PW-2 is admittedly a Surgeon and not Neurologist.
Assessment by PW-2 of disability of mind would be incapable of being assessed by him.

However, CT Scan report at Ex.P8 and discharge summary at Ex.P9 and Medicolegal Certificate would indicate that claimant had sustained fracture of:
(a) BONE WINDOW:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 "E/o Communited Fracture noted in Frontal bone with involvement of Orbital plate of Frontal bone Bilaterally - Rt.
Fontal bone # is depressed.

# medial wall of Orbit Bilaterally - with # Greater wing of Sphenoid on Rt.
Side.
Communited # in the region of Cribifrom plate of ethemoid."

(b) Scan report also makes following references:
"Multiple Hypo-Hyperdense areas - (8mm to 10mm in diameter) noted in Bifrontal region (more on Rt. side) with hyperdensity area in the corpus callosum (50mm X 14mm) - S/o Multiple Areas of Haemorrhagic Contusions in Bifrontal region and also bleed in the Corpus callosum in midline with diffuse Axonal injury.
Thin Acute Extra - dural Haematoma noted in Rt. Frontal region - 48mm X 6mm (thickness).
E/o SAH along the Falx, Tentorium and in bilateral high Parietal Cortical Sulci.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6478 Ventricles appears mildly compressed bilaterally - No e/o midline shift.
Effacement of Cortical sulci with reduced density of brain parenchyma - s/o Mild to Moderate Cerebral Odema - No e/o Odema of brain stem.

Post. Fossa structures appear grossly normal."
12.

Though PW-2 is a General Surgeon and not a Neuro Surgeon, referring to injuries and changes in brain pattern noted in scan report, even in absence of expert evidence regarding disability, based on available material, notional disability/loss of earning capacity could be assessed.
From award it is seen that tribunal accepted medical bills to extent of Rs.4,15,700/- produced and awarded same.

When tribunal accepted treatment taken by claimant, it would be safe to assume loss of earning Arif S/O Razaksab Bilagi vs Mohammed Hanif S/O Hussainsab Bahaddur ... on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66587699/
4 capacity at 6%.

sentences.text:
Thus, claimant would be entitled for future loss of income as:
Rs.6,500/- X 6% X 12 X 18 = Rs.84,240/-.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.

Considering number of fractures,
it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.65,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during laid- up period for three months.
Considering fact that claimant had sustained head injury, it would be appropriate to consider loss of earning during four months, which would be Rs.26,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Since loss of earning capacity is taken at 6%, compensation towards of loss of amenities can be granted at Rs.25,000/-.
Claimant has taken inpatient treatment for period of 50 days at Solapur and Vijayapura etc.
Considering same, it would be appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- towards attendance and other incidental expenses.
Award of Rs.4,15,700/- towards medical bills which is in complete reimbursement is maintained.
Thus, claimant would be entitled for total reassessed compensation of Rs.6,45,940/-.
Hence, point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. Claimant is held entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,45,940/- with interest at 6% per annum from claim petition till deposit (Excluding period of 388 days as per order dated 25.07.2017).
iii. Insurer is held liable to pay same and shall deposit it within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. On deposit, 40% to be kept in fixed deposit for period of two years in any Nationalized Bank of choice and remaining 60% is ordered to be released to claimant.
